questionText: Priyanka's stock portfolio consists of three stocks. The first stock represents 25% of the portfolio and generates a return of 5%. The second stock represents 40% of the portfolio and generates a return of 10%. The third stock represents the remaining portion and generates a negative return of 2%. What is the average return of the portfolio?
A shopkeeper marks a toy at ₹500 and gives a 10% discount. If he still earns 25% profit, what was the cost price?
solutionText: Selling price = ₹500 - 10% = ₹450. If CP = x and profit = 25%, then 1.25x = 450, so x = 360. Wait, note: selling price to CP ratio should be 1.25, so CP = 450 / 1.25 = ₹360. Hence the correct answer is ₹360.

questionText: Asif, a retailer sold two mobile phones at the rate of ₹6000 each, one at a profit of 20% and the other at a loss. He incurred a loss of 4% in the whole transaction. What is the loss percentage on the mobile which was sold at a loss?
solutionText: CP of first phone = 6000/1.20 = ₹5000. Total SP = ₹12000. Since overall loss is 4%, total CP = 12000/0.96 = ₹12500. CP of second phone = 12500 − 5000 = ₹7500. Loss = 7500 − 6000 = ₹1500. Loss% = 1500/7500 × 100 = 20%.
